clinician.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old Asian male presented with a 2-month history of symmetrical swelling localized to the dorsum of both hands with characteristic pitting edema, joint tenderness, and restricted bilateral proximal interphalangeal joint movement. The swelling was unresponsive to loop diuretic therapy (furosemide 40 mg daily). Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 118 mm/hour, CRP 6.58 mg/dL) and slight anemia (hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL). Plain radiographs of both hands demonstrated soft tissue swelling without joint space narrowing or bone erosion. Based on the characteristic clinical presentation of symmetrical dorsal hand swelling with pitting edema in an elderly patient, elevated inflammatory markers, and imaging findings consistent with inflammatory arthritis without erosive changes, the diagnosis of RS3PE was established. Treatment with prednisolone 15 mg daily was initiated, resulting in dramatic clinical improvement with complete resolution of hand swelling and normalization of inflammatory markers (ESR and CRP returned to normal) at 1-week follow-up, confirming the diagnosis.

final.final_diagnosis: Bilateral RS3PE (Remitting Seronegative Symmetrical Synovitis with Pitting Edema)
final.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old Asian male presented with a 2-month history of symmetrical swelling localized to the dorsum of both hands with characteristic pitting edema, joint tenderness, and restricted bilateral proximal interphalangeal joint movement. The swelling was unresponsive to loop diuretic therapy (furosemide 40 mg daily). Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 118 mm/hour, CRP 6.58 mg/dL) and slight anemia (hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL). Plain radiographs of both hands demonstrated soft tissue swelling without joint space narrowing or bone erosion. Based on the characteristic clinical presentation of symmetrical dorsal hand swelling with pitting edema in an elderly patient, elevated inflammatory markers, and imaging findings consistent with inflammatory arthritis without erosive changes, the diagnosis of RS3PE was established. Treatment with prednisolone 15 mg daily was initiated, resulting in dramatic clinical improvement with complete resolution of hand swelling and normalization of inflammatory markers (ESR and CRP returned to normal) at 1-week follow-up, confirming the diagnosis.
